evidence.why: Exact field, branch order and outgoing selector.
Predicate consumes the B3 command bit.
Captain-only selector-3 motion route and held-item assertion.

facts.rationale: Corrects the stale input field and records the predicate's side effect and downstream restriction.
facts.value: Reads Fighter.input.held_buttons[0]; absence of HSD_PAD_A clears mv.co.swing.x0. It then evaluates ftCheckThrowB3 before the latch test. That inline consumes a set throw_flags_b3 even when x0 is zero. Only a true predicate and nonzero latch forward gobj with selector 3 to ftCo_Attack_800CCF58. The dispatcher asserts a held item and has a selector-3 motion path for FTKIND_CAPTAIN, asserting for other fighter kinds.

evidence.why: Dispatch is constrained rather than universally successful.

facts.rationale: Preserves the one-way latch invariant without overstating continuous input or universal continuation.
facts.value: Common entry arms mv.co.swing.x0 to 1. Each invocation that observes A absent clears it before evaluating the continuation condition; this helper never rearms it. B3 is consumed independently of latch eligibility because ftCheckThrowB3 is the left operand of &&. With a nonzero latch and consumed B3 it requests selector 3, whose successful transition depends on dispatcher preconditions. The latch tracks sampled A absence, not unobserved physical button changes between invocations.

evidence.why: Strict speed comparison and translation/friction alternatives.

facts.rationale: Records exact arithmetic and optional branch without assuming multiplier magnitude.
facts.value: Reads mv.co.swing.x4. Exactly 4 forwards gobj, p_ftCommonData->x420 * co_attrs.ground_friction, and facing_dir to ft_80085030; the comma expression (0, ground_friction) yields ground_friction. All other values call ft_80084FA8, which multiplies the character friction by friction_when_above_walk_speed only when the computed ground-speed magnitude exceeds walk_max_vel. ft_80085030 either derives acceleration from translation offset when x594_b0 is set or applies the supplied friction, then calls ftCommon_ApplyGroundMovement.

evidence.why: Strict threshold and alternate acceleration branch.

facts.rationale: Qualifies boundary behavior and avoids the unsupported assertion that friction must increase or always be applied.
facts.value: Selector 4 chooses the x420-scaled friction argument; every other integer chooses ordinary speed-sensitive friction selection. Equality with walk_max_vel does not trigger the ordinary multiplier. The downstream x594_b0 branch ignores the friction argument and derives translation-driven acceleration instead; both branches perform grounded movement. This helper contains no explicit motion-state transition or validation of floating inputs, and neither multiplier's numerical effect is established here.

evidence.why: Synchronous ordered calls and absence of validation/storage.

facts.rationale: Exact control flow and callback lifetime contract are stronger than an unconditional ordinary-Fall outcome claim.
facts.value: Calls ft_800827A0 and skips the remaining operations if its result is nonzero. On zero it synchronously calls cb(gobj), then calls ftCo_Fall_Enter if cb returns normally. It neither stores nor null-checks cb, and performs no post-callback object validation or cancellation test. The callback must be callable on this branch and leave gobj valid for Fall processing. The collision predicate can mutate positions on either result; Fall entry can select specialized routes instead of ordinary Fall.

facts.rationale: Summarizes every owned lifecycle function while preserving consuming commands, optional callbacks and delegated transitions.
facts.value: Entry clears throw flags, supplies the selected motion with zero start/blend arguments and caller speed, processes animation, arms swing.x0, stores the selector in swing.x4, and dispatches optional fighter-kind item-drop handling. IASA clears the latch when sampled A is absent, consumes B3 even if disarmed, and requests selector 3 only when eligible; the dispatcher restricts its motion route. Animation exhaustion calls the neutral-routing helper then optional pickup handling. Selector 4 chooses x420-scaled friction, with translation-driven acceleration possible downstream. Collision predicate failure synchronously invokes cleanup before Fall entry. The generic cleanup dispatches pickup handling only if the current item pointer is non-null.
